reasoning_traces.think:
The framework introduces two distinct stochastic processes: xS models shot generation as a Bernoulli event per second, while xG models shot conversion as a conditional Bernoulli. Their product xG+_t = xS_t × xG_t defines a joint expectation for goal-scoring opportunities. This dual decomposition allows for separate calibration of attempt frequency and quality. In GSE, this translates to modeling play initiation (xS) and execution (xG) as distinct state transitions. The aggregation rules—either 'at-least-one' or 'max-per-possession'—define how these per-frame expectations combine into possession-level metrics. Dualities emerge in that xS can be interpreted as a proxy for offensive pressure, whereas xG reflects defensive vulnerability. Failure modes include temporal autocorrelation due to shuffled cross-validation, which violates causality in sequential data. Additionally, the model assumes stationarity of xS and xG over time, which may not hold under changing tactical setups or player fatigue.
